text:
sam_support: Customer reported internal API resolving to NXDOMAIN after peering with shared-services VPC. Error shows up in app logs as DNS lookup failed for storage.internal.example.com :-(

eva_sre: Oof. Was this working before peering?

sam_support: Yes — tenant said fine until we created VPC peering yesterday. Only internal svc endpoints broken, public APIs fine.

eva_sre: Can you paste a quick repro (dig + curl) from a pod in the tenant VPC?

sam_support: Sure. From pod: 
```
$ dig +short storage.internal.example.com @10.0.0.2

# returns nothing (NXDOMAIN)
$ dig +trace storage.internal.example.com
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> +trace storage.internal.example.com
;; global options: +cmd
;; Received 2 queries, 1 answers
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 4321
```

sam_support: Also tried curl to IP of known healthy instance in shared-services, connection times out when using service DNS name, works by IP.

jordan_infra: My first guess: overlapping Route53 private hosted zones between tenant account and shared-services account. When peering and resolver rules are applied, the resolver may choose the wrong hosted zone or cache a negative response. Can you confirm hosted zones?

mike_eng: I checked in infra-console: shared-services owns private zone "internal.example.com" (zone-id ZSVC12345), tenant previously had a delegated subzone "tenant.internal.example.com" (ZTNT67890). When peering, both zones associated to the same VPC in shared-services account. That can create ambiguity.

tenant_admin: We intentionally created a private hosted zone in tenant for tenant.internal.example.com for a migration. Didn't realize it would overlap after peering.

ops-bot: Incident created: I-2026-4527. Assigning to eng-infra and eng-sre.

eva_sre: Repro steps that help debug to surface race/caching: 1) From tenant pod, run `dig @10.0.0.2 storage.internal.example.com +norec` 2) From shared-services resolver, run same 3) check Route53 ListHostedZonesByName for internal.example.com in both accounts 4) check VPC associations.

mike_eng: Observed behaviour: sometimes initial resolve returns NXDOMAIN then subsequent resolve returns correct A because the local coredns (in shared-services) had cached a negative response from the tenant resolver before the hosted zone association fully propagated. Looks like an ordering problem where peering created, query forwarded to tenant resolver which had no record for the full zone and returned NXDOMAIN, that negative cached in the shared-services resolver.

jordan_infra: Workaround options: 
- Disassociate the tenant private zone from the shared-services VPC (so only the authoritative hosted zone remains) OR
- Add an outbound resolver rule in tenant account to forward internal.example.com queries to the shared-services resolver endpoints (prevent tenant returning NXDOMAIN) OR
- Clear DNS caches (restart coredns pods / flush daemon) while we fix hosted zone associations.

sam_support: Tenant applied quick workaround: removed association of tenant.private zone from shared-services VPC. After ~30s, core DNS started resolving correctly. Customer reports recovery.

eva_sre: Permanent fix: consolidate zone ownership for overlapping namespaces. For future peering, add pre-checks in onboarding to detect private-hosted-zone overlaps and warn/orchestrate disassociation steps. Filing infra task.

jordan_infra: Filed infra task INFRA-1987 to add pre-check + automation. Also adding a health check in onboarding that runs `ListHostedZones` and flags overlapping names.

sam_support: Closing loop with customer and adding notes to ticket. Will follow up on TTL/caching guidance and restart playbook.

mike_eng: Side note: if anyone hits TLS cert verification errors after this, check that the SNI name matches the host that ended up resolving. If clients end up hitting the wrong backend IP during the race, they might get a cert for another service -> TLS name mismatch.

tenant_admin: Thanks all — appreciate the clear repro and the quick workaround.

ops-bot: Incident I-2026-4527 marked resolved.
